Scope: the problem (valuing a private company), what a comp is, and our answer in a paragraph. The focus is
whether comp B matches target A; EV/EBITDA is context, reported once in @sec-results.

Facts available:

- `f.n_supplied` = `{python} f.n_supplied`: companies supplied
- `f.n_universe` = `{python} f.n_universe`: companies kept (the universe)
- `f.n_training` = `{python} f.n_training`: training companies (comp pool and development targets)
- `f.n_holdout` = `{python} f.n_holdout`: holdout companies
- `f.n_facets` = `{python} f.n_facets`: general facets per company
- `f.n_traits` = `{python} f.n_traits`: economic traits per company (E1-E10)
- `f.n_labelled_pairs` = `{python} f.n_labelled_pairs`: target-comp pairs graded by at least one reviewer (in-universe comps only)
- `f.n_labelled_targets` = `{python} f.n_labelled_targets`: targets in those pairs
- `f.n_labelled_twice` = `{python} f.n_labelled_twice`: of those pairs, graded by two or more reviewers
- `f.n_reviewers` = `{python} f.n_reviewers`: reviewers
